facts.text: Baldwyn grew from Carrollville when the Mobile and Ohio Railroad bypassed the original village, prompting citizens to relocate and name the new town after the surveyor.
The town officially incorporated on April 1, 1861, following its founding on November 20, 1860.
Baldwyn sits on the Lee–Prentiss county line, with its main street stretching five miles north of Guntown.
Every two years, the Brice’s Crossroads Museum Commission stages an elaborate living‑history encampment featuring blacksmithing, soapmaking, and period merchandise.
A 1942 tornado razed many historic buildings, but the community rebuilt, preserving its heritage in a downtown mural.
Baldwyn is a Certified Local Government and Main Street Community, celebrating its past through a downtown mural that chronicles historic events.
